title: 審議会は「下請け」か　裁量労働制の見直し、官邸主導に連合反発
extracted_text:
労働市場改革の議論のたびに噴出してきた官邸主導への不満が再び表面化してきた。「分科会が下請けのようになってしまっている」。連合の菅村裕子総合政策推進局長は4月17日、労働政策審議会（労政審）の労働条件分科会で訴えた。

労政審は2001年の厚生労働省の発足とともに設置された、厚労相の諮問機関だ。労災保険や雇用保険など労働にまつわるテーマを網羅する。とりわけ労働条件分科会は雇用主と交渉する団体交渉権や労働契約など、根幹に関わる議論を担ってきた。

目下のテーマはあらかじめ労使で決めたみなし労働時間をもとに賃金を払う「裁量労働制」だ。高市早苗首相が2月の施政方針演説で見直しを掲げた。政府は夏にまとめる経済財政運営と改革の基本方針（骨太の方針）や成長戦略で改革の柱に据える構えだ。

いまは証券アナリストや金融商品開発といった20職種と、事業の企画、立案、調査、分析の4つの業務に限っている。経団連は生産性の底上げにつながるとして対象業務の拡大を求めてきた。鉄道や信号システムを顧客に提案する交渉業務などが念頭にある。連合は長時間労働の温床になるとして強く反対してきた。

菅村氏が危機感をあらわにしたのは、首相の方針が経済界の意向に沿うと映ったからだけではない。政府が検討のメインステージに据えたのが、労政審ではなく内閣官房が主導する日本成長戦略会議だったからだ。

成長戦略会議では「労働市場改革分科会」という名の会議で議論を進めている。事務局は厚労省が担う。11人のメンバーのうち労働者側は連合の神保政史事務局長のみで、経済団体側の2人より少ない。ほかは大学教授やエコノミスト、企業の人事担当者らだ。

「職場実態を熟知した労使を含む3者構成の原則を踏まえた、労政審の議論を尊重すべきだ」。菅村氏は強調する。

戦後の労働政策は労働組合と使用者団体、学識者による意思決定を原則としてきた。国際労働機関（ILO）の原理を踏まえたもので、それぞれの意見を平等に反映する狙いがある。労働条件分科会も3者が8人ずつ参加する。

3者構成はかねて批判の的になってきた。例えば政府の規制改革会議の作業部会は07年の意見書で「政策決定の要の審議会であるにもかかわらず意見分布の固定化という弊害を持っている」と労政審に言及した。

こうした潮流が強まったのは01年に小泉純一郎政権が発足し、政策形成を官邸が主導するようになってからだ。

成長戦略会議の分科会メンバーを務める法政大の山田久教授は「労使自治の下ではバブル経済崩壊で増えた非正規労働者が抱える問題を解決しづらくなり、政治が介入せざるを得なくなった」とみる。

官邸主導にくさびを打ち込んだこともある。第2次安倍晋三政権での働き方改革の議論では繁忙月の残業時間の上限について、経済界が推した「100時間以下」から最終的に「100時間未満」に下がった。官邸に設置された会議のメンバーだった連合の神津里季生会長（当時）が反発したからだ。

「改めて、裁量労働制の拡充は不要であると申し上げたい」。連合が29日に都内で開いたメーデー中央大会。芳野友子会長は出席した首相の横で声を張り上げた。

労政審の枠組みで抵抗を続けるのか、3者構成を飛び出して打開策を探るのか。芳野氏の挙動が注目される。

【関連記事】
translated_text:
Discontent toward prime minister's office-led initiatives, which has repeatedly emerged during labor market reform discussions, has surfaced once again. "The subcommittee has become like a subcontractor." Yuko Sugimura, Rengo's General Policy Promotion Bureau Chief, stated on April 17 at the Labor Policy Council's Labor Conditions Subcommittee.

The Labor Policy Council was established in 2001 along with the creation of the Ministry of Health, Labor and Welfare, serving as an advisory body to the minister. It covers topics related to labor, including workers' accident insurance and employment insurance. The Labor Conditions Subcommittee, in particular, has handled fundamental discussions on collective bargaining rights and labor contracts negotiated between employers and workers.

The current issue at hand is the "discretionary work system" in which wages are paid based on presumed working hours predetermined by labor and management. Prime Minister Sanae Takaishi presented the review of this system during her policy speech in February. The government intends to make it a pillar of reform in its economic and fiscal management basic policy guidelines ("bone-heavy policy") and growth strategy to be compiled this summer.

Currently, it is limited to 20 job types such as securities analysts and financial product development, as well as four business categories: business planning, planning, research, and analysis. The Keidanren (Japanese Business Federation) has sought to expand the eligible occupations, arguing it would boost productivity. This includes negotiation work proposing railways and signal systems to customers. Rengo has strongly opposed this, saying it would become a hotbed for long working hours.

The reason Sugimura expressed a sense of crisis is not only that the prime minister's policy appeared to align with business interests. The government designated the Japan Growth Strategy Council, led by the Cabinet Office rather than the Labor Policy Council, as the main venue for its review.

At the Growth Strategy Council, discussions are advanced in a meeting called the "Labor Market Reform Subcommittee." The secretariat is handled by the Ministry of Health, Labor and Welfare. Among the 11 members, only one from the labor side—Masafumi Jimbo, Rengo's Secretary General—which is fewer than the two members from economic organizations. The rest are university professors, economists, and corporate human resources personnel.

"We should respect the Labor Policy Council's discussions based on the three-party composition principle, involving labor and management who are thoroughly familiar with actual workplace conditions." Sugimura emphasized.

Postwar labor policy has generally adopted a decision-making principle involving labor unions, employer organizations, and academics. This is based on the International Labour Organization (ILO) principles, aiming to equally reflect each opinion. The Labor Conditions Subcommittee also consists of eight participants from each of the three parties.

The three-party composition has long been a target of criticism. For example, a working group of the government's Regulatory Reform Council noted in its 2007 opinion paper that "despite being a key council for policy decision-making, it suffers from the drawback of fixed opinion distribution," referring to the Labor Policy Council.

This trend strengthened when the Junichiro Koizumi administration was launched in 2001, with the prime minister's office taking the lead in policy formation.

Professor Hisashi Yamada of Hosei University, who serves on the Growth Strategy Council's subcommittee, believes that "under labor-management autonomy, it becomes difficult to solve the problems of non-regular workers who increased after the bubble economy collapse, making political intervention unavoidable."

The prime minister's office has also driven wedges into this issue. During discussions on work style reform under the second Abe administration, regarding overtime hour limits during busy months, the limit was ultimately lowered from the business-backed "100 hours or less" to "less than 100 hours." This was because Riko Kozo, then president of Rengo who was a member of the council established at the prime minister's office, opposed it.

"Once again, we maintain that expansion of the discretionary work system is unnecessary." At Rengo's May Day central rally held in Tokyo on the 29th, President Tomiko Yoshino raised her voice beside the prime minister.

Whether to continue resisting within the Labor Policy Council framework or to break out of the three-party composition and seek a breakthrough—attention is focused on Yoshino's actions.
title_en: Is Council Becoming 'Subcontractor'? Rengo Opposes PM's Office-Led Reform of Discretionary Work System
